question: Should OpenClaw expose a maintained OpenAPI/Swagger contract, and which Gateway surfaces are in scope for the first supported schema?
rationale: The code already has TypeBox protocol schemas and several documented HTTP APIs, but turning those into a public OpenAPI contract creates security, compatibility, and release-versioning commitments that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Approve HTTP-only schema first
options.body: Generate and optionally serve a versioned OpenAPI contract for the documented /v1 and /tools/invoke HTTP endpoints, with explicit operator-auth and exposure guidance.

options.title: Design a broader protocol schema
options.body: Include WebSocket RPC and protocol payloads as well, accepting a larger compatibility and schema-generation project.

options.title: Decline core OpenAPI for now
options.body: Keep the current docs and TypeBox exports as the supported contract until a maintainer sponsors a narrower API reference plan.

recommendation.title: Approve HTTP-only schema first
recommendation.body: Generate and optionally serve a versioned OpenAPI contract for the documented /v1 and /tools/invoke HTTP endpoints, with explicit operator-auth and exposure guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the prior config OpenAPI draft and recent Gateway API contract work, so he is the best available owner for the scope decision.
